channel.title: Communications Earth & Environment
channel.description:
Communications Earth & Environment is an open access journal from Nature Portfolio that publishes high-quality research, reviews and commentary in the Earth, environmental and planetary sciences. The papers we publish represent significant advances that bring new insight to a specialized area of research. We also provide a community forum for issues of importance to Earth, environmental and planetary scientists, regardless of sub-discipline.

Our scope covers all areas of the geosciences, climate and environmental sciences as well as planetary sciences, including those at the interface with ecology, sustainability and environmental social sciences. Primary research of interest to the journal includes important insights gained from field work, novel analyses of existing data, numerical or analytical modelling, theoretical studies or laboratory experiments.

We encourage submissions that provide independent confirmation of particularly influential publications.

The submission and review processes are managed by our in-house professional editors supported by our Editorial Board Members, who provide technical expertise across the breadth of the Earth, environmental and planetary sciences. We are committed to rapid dissemination of important research results. Articles are published on a continuous basis to ensure swift communication of findings.

item.title: Englacial authigenesis in deep Antarctic ice: implications for Martian dust oxidation
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 24 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04076-9

Brines generated within deep ice can provide reactive micro-environments for geochemical reactions and dust aggregation, including potentially on Mars and other planetary ice environments, according to micro-scale observations from Antarctic ice cores.
item.dc:title: Englacial authigenesis in deep Antarctic ice: implications for Martian dust oxidation

item.title: Electromethanogenesis underpins the methane production in a Tibetan wetland
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04092-9

Direct interspecies electron transfer drives methane production in Tibetan wetlands and is more efficient than H2-dependent methanogenesis, shown using CO-inhibited microcosms, isotope tracing, electrochemistry, and electron-shuttle amendments.
item.dc:title: Electromethanogenesis underpins the methane production in a Tibetan wetland

item.title: Experimental reproduction of a surface-encircling olivine rim in barred olivine chondrules
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04083-w

Olivine rim formation in barred olivine chondrules requires the surface to be cooler than the interior, which may occur through evaporation and latent heat loss, according to experiments on simulated samples using a laser-heated gas-jet levitation system.
item.dc:title: Experimental reproduction of a surface-encircling olivine rim in barred olivine chondrules

item.title: Dissecting land subsidence along United States coasts through hazard characterization and exposure disparities
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 22 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04065-y

Most coastal areas of the United States are sinking, with the Gulf Coast and disadvantaged communities facing the highest risk, according to an analysis of more than 190 million satellite and ground-based measurements of land elevation change. The study characterizes the statistical distribution of vertical land motion rates and identifies significant subsidence clusters nationwide, providing a quantitative basis for targeted mitigation and adaptation.
item.dc:title: Dissecting land subsidence along United States coasts through hazard characterization and exposure disparities

item.title: Arctic lightning during solar wind disturbance
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 22 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04074-x

Solar wind intensity has a sporadic and regionally heterogeneous influence on lightning occurrence in the exposed auroral high latitude regions, according to an analysis of over 20 years of ground and space-based observations in Fennoscandia.
item.dc:title: Arctic lightning during solar wind disturbance

item.title: Power sector decarbonization increases construction phase embodied emissions in China
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 22 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04095-6

Construction phase embodied emissions from China’s power infrastructure increase under more stringent power sector climate targets, according to a study combining power system modeling with material flow and input output analyses.
item.dc:title: Power sector decarbonization increases construction phase embodied emissions in China

item.title: An early shift from wetland-adjacent to upland farming in the Maya lowlands
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 22 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04026-5

Data from Belize document a shift from wetland-adjacent maize farming at 6,000 BP to upland maize farming by 3,500 BP correlating with climate change and population growth, as shown by multiproxy palaeoecological and isotopic data that track farming and landscape disturbance.
item.dc:title: An early shift from wetland-adjacent to upland farming in the Maya lowlands

item.title: Cosmogenic radiocarbon production and glacial cycles control marine radiocarbon archive variations
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 22 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04073-y

Simulated marine radiocarbon reservoir ages range from 400 to 1200 years at the sea surface, according to 50,000 year-long earth system model simulations equipped with radiocarbon.
item.dc:title: Cosmogenic radiocarbon production and glacial cycles control marine radiocarbon archive variations
